data.text: To what extent do composite mental images in dreams rely exclusively on fragmented recollections of real sensory inputs, as Descartes suggests, versus creative synthesis generated by underlying psychological structures?

data.statement: Perceptual components in dream states and imagination draw upon foundational sensory memories, aligning psychological theories of representation with classical epistemological accounts of composite imagery.

data.position: Ubique treats the hypothesis that dream imagery is strictly derivative of real sensory components as provisional, recognizing that modern psychology explores deeper symbolic and unconscious synthesis mechanisms.
